html:
The Pemón are a Carib-speaking people of the Gran Sabana, the high grassland of south-eastern Venezuela, and nearby parts of Brazil and Guyana. They have three main branches: the Arekuna, Kamarakoto and Taurepang.

Their land is the country of the tepuis, flat-topped table mountains such as Mount Roraima and Auyán-tepui, from which Angel Falls drops. In Pemón belief the tepuis are homes of spirits and the stumps of a great tree of life. They farmed manioc, hunted and fished.

Missionaries arrived in the late 1800s and 1900s, and most Pemón became Catholic or Adventist. Since then mining for gold and diamonds has torn up their rivers. Their neighbours include the Kalina to the north and the Wapishana to the south.
